title: Wonders of Bhutan | FREE Excursion to Paro
highlights: Immerse yourself in the serene landscapes and rich culture of Bhutan, exploring destinations like Thimphu, Punakha, and Paro.
Visit the magnificent Punakha Dzong, an architectural marvel set at the confluence of the Pho Chhu and Mo Chhu (rivers), reflecting Bhutanese rich traditions.
Experience a scenic drive through Dochula Pass near Thimphu, where you'll witness stunning views of the Himalayan ranges and 108 chortens (memorial) dotting the landscape.
Witness the grandeur of Rinpung Dzong Monastery in Paro, a stunning fortress monastery with intricate Bhutanese architecture.
Embark on a hike to the iconic Tiger's Nest Monastery in Paro, perched on a cliff 3,120 metres, offering mesmerizing views and a sacred atmosphere.

know_before_you_go: Ask your local guide to help you purchase a SIM on arrival, as Bhutan supports 2 networks: B-Mobile SIM and TashiCell.
It is wise to carry enough cash, especially for remote areas in the Ngultrum (BTN) currency.

ID Proof is mandatory for each individual guest at the time of booking, and upon arrival. PAN Card will not be considered as a valid identity proof. All foreign nationals must carry their passport as a proof of identity.
Travellers aren't expected to wear the traditional kira, but you should make sure your clothing covers your arms and legs when entering a Dzong.

Indians must pay the Sustainable Development Fee (SDF) of Rs 1200 per person/per night. Children below 5 years are exempted from SDF, while kids between 6 and 12 years of age, will get 50% concession.
To obtain entry in Bhutan, Indian tourists must carry their passports with a minimum 6 months validity and make the payment of SDF.
Plastic has been banned since 1999 in Bhutan, therefore, it is advised to carry plastic/plastic items.
Keep your arms and legs covered while visiting a Dzong (fortress-monastery).
Ask for permission from the attending authority before taking any photos or videos inside places like monasteries.
In Bhutan, Tuesday is ‘Dry Day’. This means locals don’t drink alcohol on Tuesday. So it would be respectful to avoid alcohol on Tuesdays too.
It’s illegal for tobacco to be sold in Bhutan. Tourists can bring cigarettes into the country, but can only smoke them in designated places.
Bhutan does not have a micro (or nano) SIM card. So check your mobile device for SIM compatibility before visiting Bhutan.
Credit cards are widely accepted in major cities and tourist areas. However, it is recommended to carry some cash.
The official currency in Bhutan is the Bhutanese Ngultrum (BTN). It is advisable to exchange currency at banks or authorised exchange bureaus.
Images are for representation purpose only.
Please note that prices are dynamic and may change in the peak season and on blackout dates.
Please note that the timings and duration of pick-up and drop-off transfers may vary based on certain factors like traffic, weather conditions, natural calamities, etc.
Prices may fluctuate with any change in services/hotels. The difference in the cost shall be borne by the client in case of any amendment in the package due to an increase in the number of guests.

meal_plans.name: Bermuda Plan
meal_plans.description: The Bermuda meal plan offers three meals at select restaurants, including breakfast, lunch, and dinner along with drinks included. Ideal for a hassle-free, all-inclusive dining experience.

meal_plans.name: Dinner Plan
meal_plans.description: The Dinner Plan provides guests with two meals included in their stay: breakfast and dinner.

meal_plans.name: American Plan
meal_plans.description: It includes all three major meals, breakfast, lunch, and dinner for the length of your stay. Generally, the rates on this plan are higher but offer a good value for your money, and of course, added convenience.

meal_plans.name: Modified American Plan
meal_plans.description: Also known as Half Board or Half Pension meal plan. It is a modified version of the American Plan and includes a room stay with breakfast and a choice between lunch and dinner.

meal_plans.name: Continental Plan
meal_plans.description: It is where your room stay involves a daily breakfast at the hotel. The hotel can either affix its option of breakfast menu or provide in the dining area for a buffet breakfast. Also, whether the room service provides the breakfast or in a general dining area, depends from hotel to hotel.

meal_plans.name: European Plan
meal_plans.description: Only the stay is included in the rates and that you will have to pay extra for using the hotel’s dining facilities. This can be called the “Room Only” Plan.

days.title: Arrival in Siliguri | Transfer to Phuntsholing | Day at Leisure
days.desc: Upon arrival in Siliguri, get transferred to Phuntsholing. Post check in, spend the day at leisure, where you can explore the city on your own. You can admire the stunning architecture of Bhutan Gate or pay your respects at the Zangto Pelri, a serene shrine nestled in the heart of Bhutan. Also, enjoy the panoramic views from Karbandi Monastery and visit other attractions before heading back to the hotel on your own for an overnight stay.

days.title: Transfer to Thimphu | Stay & Sightseeing Tour
days.desc: Today, check out of the hotel and get driven to Thimphu. Upon arrival, check in & relax for a while. Then, embark on a sightseeing tour of Thimphu. Explore the National Memorial Chorten, where you can admire murals (wall paintings) followed by the 177-ft Buddha Dordenma Statue, overlooking the Thimphu Valley. Stop by Motithang Preserve Takin, home to Bhutan's national animal, Takin. Explore the Tashichho Dzong, Simtokha Dzong, and other attractions before returning to the hotel for a night stay.

items.title: Thimphu Sightseeing Tour with Simtokha Dzong on a Private basis

days.title: Transfer to Punakha | Punakha Sightseeing Tour
days.desc: Today, check out of your hotel and head to Punakha. En route, take a scenic stop at Dochula Pass, where you'll be treated to the breathtaking views of the Himalayas. Upon arriving in Punakha. Visit Chimi Lhakhang, famously known as the "temple of fertility,". Then, marvel at the exquisite Bhutanese architecture of Punakha Dzong, which sits majestically at the confluence of the Pho Chhu and Mo Chhu (rivers). Later, you'll be driven to your hotel for check in and overnight stay.

items.title: Punakha Sightseeing Tour on a Private basis

days.title: Transfer to Paro | Stay & Sightseeing Tour
days.desc: In the morning, check out of the hotel and board your transfer to Paro, enjoying the stunning scenery as you travel. Upon arrival, check in to your hotel and take some time to relax. Later, embark on a sightseeing tour of Paro, starting with a visit to the historic ruins of Drukgyel Dzong, where you can soak in views of the majestic Mt. Jhomolhari. Next, visit Kyichu Lhakhang, one of Bhutan's oldest temples, among other attractions. After your tour, return to your hotel for an overnight stay.

items.title: Paro Sightseeing Tour on a Private basis

days.title: Day Trip to Tiger’s Nest Monastery
days.desc: Start the day by boarding a transfer to Ta Dzong, an ancient watchtower that now serves as the museum. Visit the Rinpung Dzong Monastery, known for its intricate architecture. Finally, head to Satsam Chencho Tshongkhang (starting point) for a scenic hike to Taktsang Monastery, perched on a cliff. As you ascend through lush pine forests, take in the scenic landscape before reaching the monastery to witness its sacred halls. Conclude the day by getting driven to the hotel for an overnight stay.

items.title: Tigers Nest Hiking | Bhutan on a Private basis

days.title: Transfer to Siliguri | Departure Day
days.desc: On this day, check out of the hotel and get transferred to the Siliguri Airport/Railway Station for your onward journey. This is where your trip comes to an end. Have a safe journey!
